title: Lavandula angustifolia  essential oil nanoemulsion: physicochemical characterization, enhanced antimicrobial and antibiofilm activities, antioxidant and anticancer effects, and molecular insights
content: This study investigated the formulation, physicochemical characteristics, and multifunctional biological activities of a Lavandula angustifolia essential oil nanoemulsion (LN). The nanoemulsion was prepared using Tween 80 by ultrasonication, yielding a Z-average hydrodynamic diameter of 87.4 nm, a polydispersity index (PDI) of 0.18, and a zeta potential of −31.88 mV, indicating a relatively uniform nanoscale dispersion. Transmission electron microscopy (TEM) revealed predominantly spherical droplets ranging from 17 to 32 nm. GC-MS analysis identified linalyl acetate (35.56%) and linalool (13.3%) as the major constituents of the essential oil. Biological evaluation demonstrated that LN generally exhibited greater antimicrobial activity than the conventional emulsion, with lower MIC values and larger inhibition zones against the tested microorganisms. Furthermore, LN demonstrated concentration-dependent inhibition of biofilm biomass and improved DPPH radical-scavenging activity, with an IC50 of 5.9 µg mL−1 compared with 26.6 µg mL−1 for the native emulsion. Cytotoxicity evaluation revealed IC50 values of 162.2 µg mL−1 against MCF-7 breast cancer cells and 885.9 µg mL−1 against normal Wi-38 cells, corresponding to a preliminary in vitro selectivity index of 5.46. Molecular docking suggested potential interactions of linalool and linalyl acetate with DNA gyrase subunit B and Bcl-2. Collectively, these findings demonstrate the biological potential of the formulated L. angustifolia essential oil nanoemulsion and provide a basis for further investigations involving formulation controls, storage stability, comparative cytotoxicity, and experimental validation of the predicted molecular interactions.
